headline: Highest risk is medium: shared file-based workflows can create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error paths, but both agents are local-only with no network egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Great Expectations can read and write files for data sources, validation results, and documentation, while Pathway exposes no clipboard/MCP bridge and no direct ingestion channel is documented. The plausible interaction is file-based: if Pathway consumes Great Expectations outputs from a shared workspace, attacker-controlled content could be treated as instructions. Uncertainty about the exact bridge pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Pathway ingests Great Expectations output files from a shared directory
IF those files are parsed as instructions or prompts rather than inert data
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Treat Great Expectations outputs as data-only and strip instruction-like text
Add a manual review step before Pathway consumes generated files
Disable any file auto-discovery on the Pathway side
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for generated artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Great Expectations touches validation results and documentation, and Pathway has no filesystem read, clipboard, screen capture, or API calls listed. With no shared workspace or outbound network on either side, a leakage path is not evident from the profiles. The remaining risk is limited to manual transfer of files, which is small and avoidable.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies validation results into Pathway
IF the copied files contain sensitive validation data
mitigations: Avoid copying validation outputs into Pathway
Redact sensitive fields before any handoff
Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Use synthetic test data for integration checks

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Great Expectations can install packages and write files, but Pathway cannot write files, modify git state, or execute shells. There is no overlapping mutable surface in the profiles, so direct write-write conflict is absent. Any conflict would require an external orchestrator to grant Pathway additional rights not shown here.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants Pathway write access not shown in the profile
IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory
mitigations: Do not share a writable git checkout
Run Great Expectations package installs in an isolated environment

D_cascading_error.rationale: Great Expectations produces validation results that Pathway could plausibly consume as downstream inputs, but Pathway is not documented as critically evaluating or verifying those outputs. If Pathway treats those results as authoritative, a bad validation artifact can cascade into incorrect processing or reporting. The interaction is inferred rather than directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Pathway consumes Great Expectations validation results automatically
IF Pathway does not verify those results against source data
mitigations: Insert a verification step before Pathway consumes results
Require schema checks on Great Expectations outputs
Flag unexpected validation failures for manual review
Keep downstream actions read-only until reviewed

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent. Great Expectations is open-source with no secrets handled, and Pathway exposes no compliance-specific data classes or outbound APIs in the profile. Without a documented compliance divergence, a breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF future deployment assigns regulated data to either agent under different policies
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair until policies are reviewed
